summary: Regression test for blank-page bug on wedding invitation site. Opened site with #open shortcut, verified every section (hero, invitation, countdown, family, venue, footer) renders with computed opacity=1, non-zero height and expected text content. All [data-reveal] children within every section report opacity=1, confirming the ScrollReveal MutationObserver + safety-net fix correctly reveals late-mounted Countdown content. Countdown numbers are live (81 DAYS / 03 HOURS / 42 MINUTES / ~34 SECONDS). Confirmed removed sections (.site-nav, .music-player, events, gallery, rsvp) are absent. Floating petals layer present. Scroll-to-top keeps hero visible with names Rishabh & Ritul and date 04 DECEMBER 2026.
critical_code_review_comments: ScrollReveal fix using MutationObserver + fresh-query safety net is a robust pattern for late-mounted content; consider disconnecting the MutationObserver after the safety-net timeout to free resources.
Countdown rendering '00' placeholders before first tick is correct — avoids null-return that previously escaped the initial IntersectionObserver scan.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Blank-page bug is fixed. Site is a single-page public preview at REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL. Use '#open' hash to shortcut envelope. All section data-testids: hero-section, invitation-section, countdown-section (with countdown-days/hours/minutes/seconds), family-section, venue-section, site-footer. Removed and must NOT reappear: navbar, music player, events, gallery, rsvp.
rca of the issue: Original ScrollReveal queried [data-reveal] elements once at mount. Countdown returned null until its first timer state initialized, so its reveal children mounted AFTER the initial scan and were never observed -> stayed at opacity 0 -> visually blank region. Fix: (1) MutationObserver watches for newly added [data-reveal] nodes and observes them; (2) 2.5s safety-net re-query catches anything missed; (3) Countdown now renders structure with '00' placeholders on first render instead of returning null.
